TEXTS NOT READY. Fix first N1, N3, N4, N2; the rest are optional. All 24 earlier findings on these two pages were taken up; two (out:C5, dq:D4) are only partly repaired.

Case page, read cold: questions 1, 2, 3, 8 and 9 can be used as written. Question 5 would be misread (a reader whose successors each draw what the parent drew answers yes, and that is question 4's case). Question 7's second sentence cannot be followed. Questions 4 (the rule), 6 and 7 lean on "the line", "the turn", "corrects" and "overdraws", none said before use. Its header's "six places … corrected here" will be stale after this round.

Direction page, from "What we have found so far" alone. What changed on 16 November: visible in the model bullet, the handed-in bullet and the last bullet; not inside the rule bullet, dated "15 and 16 November" as one. What is still given: said at each law, except that every unit needs something in "Where it holds" (N2), and misplaced in "What makes a difference" (N1). What was not reached: said once, in the last sentence of the handed-in bullet; that no rule was built on the units appears only as a description ("has no rule and no share in it").

As out:D3.

Case: "Where the level is not read, the rule is set again from the share. *A worked course: …*"

As out:C1.

new_findings.text_says: "Who comes next depends on which needs the level meets, and on nothing else where every unit leaves offspring."
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `after_alike` has no premise: levels that meet the same needs leave the same next way. Only the converse needs `leaves`; `alike_iff` docstring: "Without `leaves` only right to left holds". The rewrite conditions the half that is unconditional.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Who comes next depends only on which needs the level meets. Where every unit leaves offspring the converse holds too: levels that meet different needs leave different next ways.

new_findings.text_says: "Where offspring take the same and need no more, and every unit leaves some, the line goes on without end exactly where…"
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `unending_iff_holds (even) (some) (down) (needs : Needing need kids w) (nothing) (high) (along)`. With a unit that needs nothing, "exactly" fails: need 0, takes 1, nothing given, level 0 goes on for ever and never holds (my hand check, not Lean). The sub-bullet above lists this premise, so its absence reads as not needed.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Where offspring together take the same and need no more, every unit leaves some and needs something, and nothing comes back from nothing, the line goes on without end exactly where…

new_findings.text_says: Question 5: "If every member's successors draw exactly what it drew" … "A draw that shrinks is not covered."
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `even : ∀ u, taken use (kids u) = use u`: the successors together. Two successors each drawing the parent's draw are question 4's case. The total draw does shrink when members stop, and that is covered (`WayOfUnits.unending_iff_holds` is the case of units that only stop).
new_findings.proposed_wording: 5. If every member's successors together draw exactly what it drew, where does it come to hold? … Successors that together draw less than their parent are not covered.

new_findings.text_says: Question 7: "…reaches up to a level that the level never passes after the turn, or from which every rule holds it." … "a first reading later than that corrects and the line still ends."
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `low : N ≤ H₂ + y₂`, `covers : c ≤ K`, `safe`: from `c` up to `hi` every way's step leaves the level between `c` and `hi`. The right side fails where the first step read leaves the level below `H₂ + y₂`. True to the Lean, but "the turn" is said nowhere, "later than that" has no antecedent, and a cold reader cannot parse it.
new_findings.proposed_wording: …only if the band starts at or below that point, and its top is a level from which the level does not fall back under any rule, or one the level never reaches. … Under those conditions, a first reading that leaves the level below that point still corrects the rule, and it ends.

new_findings.text_says: "the end of the line"; "the line ended"; "after the turn"; "reads the level and corrects"; "a start that already overdraws"; "adds to its share".
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: None is said before use; "line" is also "a line of descent" in question 9. In the Lean the overdraw is `below : x < H₁ + y₁` with the floor `draws`: the start is already below the point of no return of the draw it keeps. A share of what is not said.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Add under "What the questions are about": "At some levels a reading sets the rule; the rule it sets is the corrected rule, with one fixed draw, and the step where that first happens is the turn. It overdraws when its level is already below the point of no return (question 2) of the draw it keeps." Say what the share is a share of. Write "it ends" for "the line ends".

new_findings.file: both pages (case question 4; direction, "Used up while nothing yet differs")
new_findings.text_says: "the level at that step is below something the start could meet"; "the level by then is below something the start could meet."
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `falls_to_unmet`: `∃ p, p ∈ w ∧ need p ≤ x ∧ (course … n).2 < need p`, and `(course … n).2 < x`.
new_findings.proposed_wording: the level at that step is below a need that was met at the start, and so below where it started.

new_findings.text_says: "and one test frozen beforehand still fires"; "Two sentences of the idea now have a proved form" over three sub-bullets; "(15 and 16 November)"; "the rule is read off the share again".
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: The frozen test A(3) is "holds unchanged with the stock removed": the clause before it said again, and "fires" is unexplained. The third sub-bullet is not one of the two sentences, and the second is marked a reading. New on the 16th in the rule bullet: the ending with no overdraw asked, and the reading that sets the share. "Read off" sits beside "the level is read"; the tracked page had "set again from the share".
new_findings.proposed_wording: "…hold with the stock taken out, which a test fixed beforehand named as nothing having changed." "Two sentences of the idea are read onto theorems of one small model, and a third theorem says where such a line holds." Mark the two results of the 16th. "the rule is set again from the share."

new_findings.text_says: "What selects is given there"; "are handed in"; "The one model did not reach it"; "In the one model it is handed in." Also "two levels that meet the same needs leave the same next way" beside the first sub-bullet, and readers who had not written the proof in two sections.
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: One fact said in four sections, two others twice. The page asks for each thing said once.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Keep it in "found" and "next"; drop the added sentence under "What we do not know"; in the handed-in bullet write "as said above" for the alikeness clause.

new_findings.text_says: "Who comes next depends on which needs the level meets, and on nothing else where every unit leaves offspring."
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `after_alike` has no premise: levels that meet the same needs leave the same next way. `alike_iff (leaves : ∀ u, u ∈ w → kids u ≠ [])` adds the converse; without it, levels that meet different needs can leave the same way (`AlikeFiner`). The premise sits on the half that needs none, and the half that needs it is not said.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Who comes next depends only on which needs the level meets. Where every unit leaves offspring it depends on exactly that: levels that meet different needs leave different ways.

new_findings.text_says: Item 7: "It changes whether anything goes on only where such a unit is all that is left". DIRECTION.md: "A loss of something that takes nothing changes nothing in the stock or in the rest; it changes whether anything goes on only where that thing is all that is left."
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `takes_nothing (zero) (inZ : ∀ u v, Z u → v ∈ kids u → Z v)` concludes equal levels and equal ways without `Z`. `NothingTakenEnds.ending_differs` is one case. No statement concludes "only where"; it follows by an argument from `takes_nothing` and `Goes`. The direction also drops `inZ`.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Plan: "It can still change whether anything goes on: in one small case such a unit is the only one still met, and with it something goes on, without it nothing does (`NothingTakenEnds`). That this is the only way is argued from `takes_nothing`, not a Lean statement." Direction: "A loss of something that takes nothing and leaves only its like changes nothing in the stock or in the rest. In one small case it still changes whether anything goes on."

new_findings.text_says: Q7: "Where it sets the rule only, that inequality decides only if the band that is read starts at or below that point and reaches up to a level …"
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `locked_turns_in_time_on_window_iff` takes `low`, `covers`, `safe` as premises. The header of `TurningInTime`: "these laws are sufficient conditions, and whether a line can go on where no `hi` and `c` meet them is not shown". `Three.read_at_eight_ends` fails `low` only.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Where it sets the rule only, that inequality is proved to decide where the band … Where the band starts above that point, a course can meet the inequality and still end (question 6's worked course). Whether the upper condition is needed is not shown.

new_findings.text_says: Queue: "where offspring take the same and need no more than their parent, the net never ends exactly where its course comes to hold"; "(`alike_iff`, `ways_alike`, with no premise on the stock)". Plan rows 2 and 4 the same; after the table: "given that offspring take more and need no more than their parent, on a level with a ceiling and nothing given from nothing".
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `unending_iff_holds (even) (some : ∀ u, kids u ≠ []) (down) (needs) (nothing) (high) (along)`; `way_ends … (needs : ∀ u, 0 < need u)`; `alike_iff (leaves …)`. A level of nothing meets needs of nothing, and then neither law holds.
new_findings.proposed_wording: Queue: "where every unit leaves offspring that take the same and need no more than it, every unit needing something, …"; "(`alike_iff`, where every unit of the way leaves offspring; `ways_alike`; no premise on the stock)". Plan rows and paragraph: add "under item 4's premises", "under item 5's premises"; item 4: add "nothing given from nothing". Direction, "Where it holds": begin "With the same givens on needs and on what comes back,". Case row 7, the rule only: begin "As in question 6 without the share, and:".

new_findings.text_says: "The model says only when a loss changes nothing else". Case page: "favouring adds to its share"; "the draw is the share times an amount" (also the plan and direction); Q4: "and the line ends".
new_findings.lean_or_fact_says: `gone_from` also says a line once gone does not come back; `takes_nothing` is one sufficient case. `RuleCapture.Raises` is `P.le x (f x g)`: not lowered, and in question 6's course the share stays three. `count_rises (pos : 0 < u)`. `way_ends` bounds no step.
new_findings.proposed_wording: "The model says that a line once gone does not come back, and one case in which a loss changes nothing else." "favouring does not lower its share (in question 4 it adds to it)". "a positive amount". "and the line ends, at a step no theorem bounds".

new_findings.text_says: "A first draft was read by three AI readers, who found six places". Plan: "left out premises in six places … three more readers found them". Staged NOTE.md: "Three of its sentences now have a proved form in one model".
